vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-7347
vulnerability.description: nginx mp4 module: buffer over-read while calculating trak->end_offset in ngx_http_mp4_crop_stsc_data() when processing an mp4 file with unordered stsc (sample-to-chunk) atom chunks; can crash a worker process via a crafted mp4 file when the mp4 directive is in use.

statements.action_statement: Backported the official nginx.org standalone patch (https://nginx.org/download/patch.2024.mp4.txt, mirrored in this repo at build/patches/CVE-2024-7347.patch) onto the nginx 1.25.5 source tree used for this image, applied cleanly with `patch -p1` before ./configure && make (see build/Dockerfile.build and PROGRESS.md Mission 2 section for the verified apply transcript). The patch widens the `n` counter in ngx_http_mp4_crop_stsc_data() from uint32_t to uint64_t (avoiding the overflow in `(next_chunk - chunk) * samples`) and adds an explicit `next_chunk < chunk` rejection with an error log line, matching the fix shipped upstream in nginx 1.27.1/1.26.2. This is the same fix upstream ships; it is not a mitigation or workaround.
statements.impact_statement: Rationale for 'fixed' rather than a version-string bump: nginx's own reported version string is unchanged (still 'nginx/1.25.5', since this is a source-level backport rather than an upgrade to 1.27.1/1.26.2), so vulnerability scanners that match purely by package name + upstream version string (Trivy's Debian tracker, Grype's NVD/CPE range matching) cannot detect this fix from version metadata alone. We independently verified: (1) neither Trivy nor Grype flagged CVE-2024-7347 against nginx in this project's own baseline scan of the unpatched nginx:1.25-bookworm image either (see baseline-trivy.txt / baseline-grype.txt - grep for CVE-2024-7347 returns zero hits in both), so there is no 'before' finding for either scanner to suppress in the first place for this specific CVE; and (2) the --vex flag mechanics themselves do work correctly on this Trivy/Grype version pair (verified with an unrelated canary CVE that IS present in the scan output, which the --vex flag successfully suppressed in both tools - see PROGRESS.md Mission 4 section for the real command transcripts). This statement is included per standard VEX practice regardless of current scanner visibility, since it (a) documents the true fix status for human/downstream consumers of this image, (b) is the correct artifact for exactly the 'source patch without a version bump' scenario, and (c) will take effect automatically the moment either scanner's database adds CVE-2024-7347 coverage for the nginx package (Trivy currently has zero nginx-package entries in its Debian tracker at all; Grype's NVD/CPE dataset for nginx 1.25.5 covers a different set of CVEs that does not currently include this one).
